name: Saint Apollinaris
history: The first bishop of Ravenna, honoured there as a martyr since very early times. Tradition, recorded centuries later, made him a disciple sent from Antioch by Saint Peter. The great basilica of Sant’Apollinare in Classe, consecrated in 549, keeps his memory, and its apse mosaic shows him in prayer among his flock, pictured as sheep.
life: Almost nothing certain is known of Apollinaris except that he founded the Church in Ravenna and that his people honoured him as their first bishop and a witness for Christ. Saint Peter Chrysologus, preaching in Ravenna in the fifth century, spoke of him as a bishop who had suffered much for the faith, and the city built him two great churches. A later account of his life, written to support Ravenna’s dignity, tells that Peter sent him from Antioch, that he worked wonders, was repeatedly beaten and exiled, and returned each time to his flock until he died of his wounds. Whatever the details, his memory has been kept with great love. In the apse at Classe, above a field of trees, flowers and birds, he stands with his arms raised in prayer beneath a jewelled cross, the shepherd of a flock of twelve white sheep.
prayerTo: Saint Apollinaris, first shepherd of Ravenna, you suffered for your flock and would not abandon them. Pray for bishops and for all who lead the Church, for those who are exiled or driven out, and for me, that I may stand among God’s people with my hands raised in prayer. Amen.
penance: Pray today for your bishop and for the first bishops of your own diocese. Pray with your hands raised for a few moments, as Apollinaris is shown.
meditation: He is remembered not by his words but by his prayer among his people. How do others see you pray?
